messages:
ana: Heads-up — nightly run for `safety-edgecases-v2` is showing nondeterministic failures again. ~4/80 shards differ from baseline and a couple hit the 30s timeout. :eyes:

matt: ugh, saw that. any logs?

ana: pasted the failing shard output below — note the seed printed at start and the sampling divergence later.

ana: ```
START seed=42
worker=3 pid=21456 model=rwd-llama-13b-quantized
sample: expected token=125 got=130
TIMEOUT waiting for worker 3 (30.01s)
Traceback (most recent frames):
  File \"/srv/eval-harness/runner.py\", line 178, in _worker_main
    sample = sampler.sample(tokens, seed=seed)
  File \"/srv/eval-harness/sampler.py\", line 87, in sample
    probs = model.step(tokens)
KeyboardInterrupt
```

ivan: hm the seed printed is the global seed, but we spawn workers via multiprocessing.Pool without an initializer that sets per-worker seeds. Could be a race where two workers inherit the same RNG state or re-seed in the wrong order.

sara: our harness uses `multiprocessing.get_context().Pool(...)` but we default to the system start method. On linux that's "fork" which clones the RNG state — if parent advanced RNG before worker work, they end up correlated.

matt: so sometimes two workers produce correlated samples and some shards end up hitting timeouts because sampling gets stuck behind a pathological sequence? :thinking_face:

ana: yes, observed correlated token patterns across two workers in the same run. Also saw one run where `os.urandom` was called in-between and changed entropy, making behavior vary between runs.

ci-bot: nightly-evals #1945678901: job failed on shard 7, exit_code=1 — rerun queued (retry #1).

ivan: quick repro attempt locally: `python -c "from multiprocessing import Pool; import random; random.seed(42); p=Pool(4); print(p.map(lambda _: random.random(), range(4)))"` sometimes prints repeated values when using fork.

matt: can we switch to `forkserver` or `spawn`? `forkserver` avoids copying the parent's RNG because server starts fresh processes.

ana: tried `multiprocessing.get_context('forkserver')` in a branch — locally it stabilizes the outputs but CI image is older and doesn't support forkserver due to missing `multiprocessing.semaphore_tracker` fix.

sara: alternative is to set per-worker seed in initializer: Pool(initializer=_seed_worker, initargs=(global_seed,)) where `_seed_worker` calls `random.seed(global_seed + worker_id); np.random.seed(...); torch.manual_seed(...)`. That should be robust across start methods.

ivan: agree. also set `os.environ['PYTHONHASHSEED']=str(seed)` when launching eval process. And disable `cuDNN` auto-tune if we need determinism: `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False` (but that may impact perf).

matt: we should be careful — production nightly wants high throughput. If deterministic flags slow things, we only need this for nightly regression checks, not hosted inference. Maybe create a CI-only config that launches evals with deterministic seeding and smaller beam to reduce cost.

ana: created a small reproducer script in the repo: `tools/repro/multiprocess_rng_repro.py` — it demonstrates different behavior under fork vs forkserver and shows token collisions when using fork.

sara: nice. I opened a PR that implements per-worker initializer + explicit seeding and a feature flag `EVAL_DETERMINISTIC`. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/1226 (draft).

ivan: code snippet suggestion for initializer: ```def _seed_worker(rank, base_seed):
    s = (base_seed + rank) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    random.seed(s)
    np.random.seed(s % 2**32)
    torch.manual_seed(s)
    try:
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(s)
    except Exception:
        pass
```

matt: also add a test that spawns 8 workers and asserts no duplicate first-sample tokens across workers for N=1000 runs (statistical but better than nothing).

ana: CI runs with PR show failures in older ubuntu image — `forkserver` not available there. Per-worker seeding branch passes 50/50 locally; let's trigger full nightly in staging.

ci-bot: PR 1226: tests triggered on staging — job 1945678967 queued.

ivan: FYI, I also found a small bug in runner where the worker id passed to initializer was `i` from enumerate which can change if Pool resizes. Switched to `multiprocessing.current_process()._identity` as reliable source.

sara: good catch. Added that fix to the PR.

matt: long-term, we should also avoid shared-state RNG in the parent and prefer to create a fresh RNG per worker process before any model loads. Put a `before_fork` hook?

ana: agreed. Action items: (1) land per-worker seeding + current_process id fix (sara) (2) add CI-only deterministic flag and smaller config (matt) (3) run full nightly on staging and monitor diffs (ana) (4) follow up if perf regressions with cuDNN flags (ivan).

sara: I'll update PR and ping for review. :white_check_mark:

ana: thanks team — let's hope this kills the intermittent flakes. Will keep watching tonight's runs. :coffee:
